reason: Confirmed by measurement, and the two refutation grounds offered both fail. Drove master.html?v=paper in chromium with CDP Page.setFontSizes at standard 16/20/24 (no :root font-size is declared anywhere in shell.css, so rem does follow the reader; computed documentElement font-size read back 16/20/24 exactly). The reading tier scales linearly and the five display steps do not move a pixel at any root: .b-num 96px at 390 and 148px at 1440 unchanged; .b-ogNum/.b-ogWord 64px unchanged; .b-emptyTitle 64px unchanged; .b-pressTitle 48px unchanged. The seat's ratios reproduce to the decimal. Phone owner-flight, count to moment title: 96/17 = 5.65 at root 16, 96/25.5 = 3.76 at root 24. Unfurl, figure to caption: 64/15 = 4.27 to 64/22.5 = 2.84, and the caption breaks from one line (22.5px tall) to two (67.5px) at root 20 while the numeral beside it is frozen. owner-empty at 1440, headline to body: 64/17 = 3.76 to 64/25.5 = 2.51. Publish, .b-pressTitle to its caption: 48/12 = 4.00 to 48/18 = 2.67, the caption breaking to two lines. GROUND ONE FAILS - the frozen tier is not figures. --size-titleWide drives .b-pressTitle (b.css:1000, the publish headline, words) and .b-emptyTitle (b.css:970, the empty state's headline, words); --size-card drives .b-ogWord (b.css:1145) and .b-emptyTitle at sheet/full (b.css:1395); --size-count drives .b-dayCount (b.css:1181), which the file's own comment at b.css:1176 says is letters and not figures. Four of the five frozen steps carry WORDS, including the two largest sentences in the product - the publish headline and the empty state's first question. A reader who raises text size gets a 25.5px body under a 64px headline that will not move, and on publish an 18px caption under a 48px headline; the file's own thesis is the step between them. GROUND TWO FAILS - a workable, bounded remedy exists and is not a build. The seat does not propose the naive rem swap it disproved; it proposes clamp() with a measured ceiling, and the arithmetic checks out byte-identical at a 16px root (2.375rem=38, 3rem=48, 4rem=64, 6rem=96, 9.25rem=148, every one equal to today's literal and equal to the clamp floor, so nothing moves for the default reader and neither gate's numbers change), with ceilings at 48/60/80/120/180 that cap growth at roughly 1.25x. It also names the one object the freeze was actually protecting - .b-dayCount, whose 'Today' already measures the full 350px column at 390 - and pins it off the token rather than pretending the conflict does not exist. That is five token lines, one pin, two width-to-min-width swaps: polish, not a restructure, and it touches nothing the lock froze. The collateral damage is separately objective and is the part no taste argument can absorb: at 390 the hard-px lane .b-measureHead (b.css:142, width 76px, white-space nowrap) holds a rem string that measures exactly 76.0px at the default - zero slack - and spills to scrollWidth 94 at root 20 (18px out of its lane) and 113 at root 24 (37px). At desk the 84px lane (b.css:1372) spills 10px and 29px. In the print sheet .b-when overflows its 220px column by 39px at root 20 and 91px at root 24. Page-level scrollWidth stays clean, so this is strings hanging out of their own lanes and over their neighbours, not a scrollbar - which is exactly why nothing has caught it. And nothing can: grepped both gates, and neither audit.mjs nor interaction-check.mjs ever calls Page.setFontSizes or reads any root but 16, so 787 assertions and fifteen audit categories all pass on the one axis the reader personally controls. SETTLED.md carries no entry on text size, rem scaling or zoom, so this is not a re-raise. The file's comment at shell.css:116-121 documents a CAUSE, not a trade-off: it argues only that a full rem swap clips, which is true, and never accounts for what the freeze costs above the default or for the seven strings that overflow their boxes at root 20. A documented reason for a decision is not the same as a measured decision. At a 9.5 bar, on a surface whose stated audience is families opening a plan once on a phone - the population that most reliably has enlarged system text - a hierarchy that halves and labels that hang out of their lanes is a defect, not a trade-off.
sharpenedFix: Take the seat's clamp() approach as written for shell.css:129-134, since the floor of each clamp equals today's literal and the ceiling caps growth near 1.25x, which keeps the composed stage honest while letting the display tier move with the reader; pin .b-dayCount to an explicit 96px at b.css:1181 with the comment extended to say it is pinned because its word already measures the full column at 390. Handle the hard-px lanes as the higher-priority half, since they are live overflow rather than lost hierarchy: .b-measureHead width to min-width at both b.css:142 and b.css:1372, .b-behindDate likewise at b.css:499, and give .b-when in the print sheet a column that can grow or a size that clamps. Then close the blind spot rather than only the instance - add one loop to interaction-check.mjs that drives owner-flight, publish, print and unfurl through Page.setFontSizes at standard 20 and 24 and asserts two things: that no element's scrollWidth exceeds its clientWidth in the set of hard-px lanes, and that the count-to-title and headline-to-body ratios stay within 10% of their 16px values. Without that loop the same class walks back in the next time a rem string is dropped into a measured lane.
